lessons.title: Describing your home
lessons.goal: Describe your flat or house and its rooms.

tip.title: piso, departamento, apartamento
tip.body: A flat is un piso in Spain, un departamento in Mexico and Argentina, and un apartamento in many other countries (understood everywhere). Rooms change too: the living room is el salón in Spain and la sala in Latin America; a bedroom is una habitación or un dormitorio, and in Mexico often una recámara. Careful: piso also means floor or storey, so vivo en un piso en el tercer piso is perfectly normal Spanish.

lessons.title: Furniture & where things are
lessons.goal: Name furniture and say where things are in a room.

tip.title: estar + location
tip.body: Use estar to say where a specific thing is: el sofá está en el salón, las llaves están encima de la mesa. Useful place words: al lado de (next to), junto a (beside), encima de (on top of), debajo de (under), delante de (in front of), detrás de (behind). To say that something exists somewhere, use hay: al lado de la cama hay un armario. Remember de + el = del: al lado del sofá.

lessons.title: The neighbourhood
lessons.goal: Say what your neighbourhood is like, good and bad.

tip.title: lo bueno, lo malo
tip.body: A handy way to weigh things up: lo bueno es que … (the good thing is that …) and lo malo es que … (the bad thing is that …). A neighbourhood is un barrio everywhere; in Mexico City and many Mexican cities people also say la colonia. Rent is el alquiler in Spain and la renta in Mexico; los vecinos are your neighbours.

phrases.n: I live in a very quiet neighbourhood.

phrases.t: Mi colonia tiene muchos parques.

phrases.t: Mis vecinos son muy amables.

phrases.t: Lo malo es que el alquiler es muy caro.

lessons.title: Comparing & ser or estar
lessons.goal: Compare homes and describe them with ser and estar.

tip.title: más … que, tan … como
tip.body: To compare, use más + adjective + que (more … than) or menos + adjective + que (less … than): este piso es más grande que el otro. For "as … as" use tan … como: es tan caro como el otro. Four common ones are irregular: mejor (better), peor (worse), mayor (older, bigger) and menor (younger, smaller). Never say más bueno for "better". For describing a home, use ser for what it is like (es grande, es antiguo, es bonito) and estar for where it is and its current state (está en el centro, está limpio, está sucio).

story.title: Which flat?
story.intro: Ana and Pablo are looking for a flat to share in Guadalajara, Mexico, and compare two adverts.

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: Mira, Pablo, aquí hay dos departamentos. El primero está en el centro y tiene dos recámaras.
lines.n: Look, Pablo, here are two flats. The first one is in the centre and has two bedrooms.

lines.name: Pablo
lines.t: Suena bien. ¿Y cuánto es la renta?
lines.n: Sounds good. And how much is the rent?

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: Doce mil pesos al mes. Es un poco caro, pero está muy bien ubicado.
lines.n: Twelve thousand pesos a month. It's a bit expensive, but it's in a very good location.

lines.name: Pablo
lines.t: ¿Y el segundo?
lines.n: And the second one?

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: El segundo es más grande y más barato: diez mil pesos. Pero está lejos del centro.
lines.n: The second one is bigger and cheaper: ten thousand pesos. But it's far from the centre.

lines.name: Pablo
lines.t: Mmm. Yo prefiero el primero. Trabajo en el centro y no tengo carro.
lines.n: Hmm. I prefer the first one. I work in the centre and I don't have a car.

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: Sí, pero el segundo tiene jardín y es más tranquilo.
lines.n: Yes, but the second one has a garden and it's quieter.

lines.name: Pablo
lines.t: Bueno, ¿por qué no vamos a ver los dos el sábado?
lines.n: Well, why don't we go and see both on Saturday?

branch.title: A flat in Valencia
branch.scene: You're viewing a flat to rent in Valencia, Spain. Señora Ortega from the letting agency meets you at the door.
branch.name: Sra. Ortega

door.t: Buenos días. ¿Viene a ver el piso de alquiler?
door.n: Good morning. Are you here to see the flat for rent?

choices.t: Sí, buenos días. Tengo una cita a las diez.
choices.n: Yes, good morning. I have an appointment at ten.
Yes, that's right. Can we go in?

tour.t: Pase, pase. Este es el salón. Es más grande que el de los otros pisos del edificio y es muy luminoso.
tour.n: Come in, come in. This is the living room. It's bigger than in the other flats in the building and it's very bright.

choices.n: How lovely! How many bedrooms does it have?

choices.t: Uf, no me gusta nada. Es horrible.
choices.n: Ugh, I don't like it at all. It's horrible.

rude.t: Bueno… pues si no le gusta, no perdemos más tiempo. Adiós.
rude.n: Well… if you don't like it, let's not waste any more time. Goodbye.
rude.outcome: You were too blunt and the agent ended the viewing. Ask questions first and stay polite.

rooms.t: Tiene dos habitaciones y un baño completo. La cocina es pequeña, pero está totalmente equipada.
rooms.n: It has two bedrooms and a full bathroom. The kitchen is small, but it's fully equipped.

choices.n: Very good. How much is the rent?

furnished.t: Sí, tiene camas, armarios, un sofá y una mesa con sillas.
furnished.n: Yes, it has beds, wardrobes, a sofa and a table with chairs.

choices.n: Perfect. And how much is the rent?

price.t: Son novecientos euros al mes, sin gastos, y dos meses de fianza.
price.n: It's nine hundred euros a month, bills not included, and two months' deposit.

choices.n: I'm very interested. When is it available?
Nine hundred? That's outrageous! I'm leaving.

leave.t: Como quiera. En este barrio los precios son así.
leave.n: As you wish. Prices are like that in this neighbourhood.
leave.outcome: You walked out without asking about anything else. Rents in big Spanish cities can be high: compare calmly before deciding.

good.t: Está libre desde el uno de mayo. Si quiere, le preparo el contrato esta semana.
good.n: It's available from the first of May. If you like, I'll prepare the contract this week.
good.outcome: You viewed the flat, asked about the rooms and the rent, and you're getting a contract.

lessons.title: My home
lessons.goal: Describe your home and neighbourhood for 60 seconds.

culture.title: Living in a piso
culture.body: In Spanish cities most people live in flats in apartment blocks rather than in houses, and the residents share the costs of the building through la comunidad de vecinos. Many young Spaniards stay in their parents' home until their late twenties or longer, and students and young workers often compartir piso (share a flat) to afford the rent. In Mexico you'll hear departamento for a flat and recámara for a bedroom, and in big cities like Mexico City or Guadalajara         many people live in flats too, while houses are more common elsewhere.

free.n: Describe your home and your neighbourhood, and compare them with a previous home or a friend's.
free.hint: Use Vivo en un piso / una casa …, Tiene … habitaciones, La cocina es …, Mi barrio es …, Lo bueno / Lo malo es que …, Es más … que ….
free.model: Vivo en un piso en el centro de la ciudad. Tiene dos habitaciones, un salón y una cocina pequeña, pero muy luminosa. Mi barrio es muy tranquilo y está bien comunicado. Lo malo es que el alquiler es muy caro. Mi piso anterior era más grande, pero este es mejor porque está más cerca de mi trabajo.
